title: I am finally ready to show a bit of my game, looking for feedback
author: TheBigQuestion354
selftext:
I am new to game dev but have been playing tabletop games and making miniatures, terrain pieces, and even tables with built in tv's for many years now. I have been working on this game for a few months now and just wanted to see what others think of it.

I am looking specifically for feedback on the art direction, UI, combat, and just do you like it? The miniatures are mostly actual recreations of miniatures I modeled in real life. The game has no real walking or "attack" animations and instead plays as a true tabletop game with miniatures. The terrain is fully destructible and I already have about a dozen quests in the game, most of which are handwritten by me (one was a commission). It uses the SRD 5.1 by Wizards of the Coast for its ruleset but I am going to homebrew a few classes.

The opening you see is the actual board by the way. If you go to the edges of the map it is the table and your character sheet is your invetory/quest journal/character page (where you equip spells and the like).

So far my biggest challenge has actually been making models where you can change the armour.

comments.author: warpedspoon
comments.body: the zoom in from main menu to in-game is really smooth

replies.author: TheBigQuestion354
replies.body: It's actually kind of "fake" as well. It loads your top save and has that on the board ready when you boot up the game.

replies.author: fart-to-me-in-french
replies.body: very weird way to say 'yeah it works as intended' lol

replies.author: TheBigQuestion354
replies.body: It came across weird. I really meant that it was difficult to implement and I kind of had to build a fake loading screen to make it work.

comments.author: erik_33_DK13
comments.body:
Looks real cool. The only thing I'd change is the UI to be fantasy themed like Warcraft 3, Deadfire or Divine Divinity. Your UI is great and visiblity is important, but those small details are very immersive for me.

Also a question for you; are there night battles with visibility/light mechanics?

replies.author: TheBigQuestion354
replies.body: My current UI takes inspiration from Solasta and the original Baldurs Gate. There are night battles and a full day/night cycle though I still need to add visibility mechanics like disadvantage if no dark vision.

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body:
You know, yea. This is neat.

That blue title screen box clashes with the rest of the design I feel. It also looks very "default Claude UI", including the font.

In-game art looks fine. It's simple, but also detailed enough to get the point across and kinda looks like some stuff you'd see on a tabletop game.

Props on sharing something that isn't a one-prompt slop and actually looks clean and good. I'd say UI definitely needs some love right now though. Mostly just in texturing and shape to get to fit in a little better and not look as default.

replies.author: TheBigQuestion354
replies.body: I agree, I have spent a lot of time on the in game UI and literally no time on the main menu UI so it needs a lot of work and the general UI has been so hard to “deslop”. Thank you for the feedback!

comments.author: tehwave
comments.body: Neat stuff! You should add tilt shift blurring. It would sell the board feeling really well.

replies.author: TheBigQuestion354
replies.body: That sounds cool actually, I’ll look into it!

comments.author: taisui
comments.body:
People will look at the menu and text font and say "ai slop"

You need to fix those before showing more people.

comments.author: drahgon
comments.body: Yeah, I don’t love the graphics. Looks a little AI sloppy. But I really like the concept. It looks different and very interesting. I would give it a try for sure.

replies.author: TheBigQuestion354
replies.body: Can you tell me what exactly looks a little AI sloppy? I want to improve it and let it cook as much as a I can. Thank you for the feedback

replies.author: drahgon
replies.body: Mainly the menus it does the same kind of menu that is just kind of bland, generic and never really fits the game look. For instance, in a medieval game, you might make the menu like a scroll or have a wood frame or something like that you know the little touches maybe the font would be in cursive or something. Like all your creature icon boxes and then the little bottom left health bar and level thing just look like completely stock and AI. Same with the main menu. Then the board game view on the main menu again. Looks like everything was dynamically generated. Nothing really looks polished. Just everything looks a little rough around the edges. The best part is actually the background of the fireplace that looks pretty nice.

replies.author: TheBigQuestion354
replies.body:
How do the characters look? It's actually funny the background of the menu is the only AI image in the whole game but I agree, I like the style at least. Considering commissioning an artist for it. I also updated the menu since everyone had the same advice.

https://i.redd.it/eapo4p628czh1.png

replies.author: drahgon
replies.body: Well, AI is also just synonymous with like stock images so if you just asset flip a bunch of stuff it kind of also looks like AI. Menu looks better

comments.author: Eldritch-Ostrich
comments.body: Looks cool! Love the tabletop style, and destructible terrain is always fun.

comments.author: Maple-Syrup89
comments.body:
I love the continue going right into the game board, that is awesome!

I think the blue menu is a bit boring and doesn't fit the rest of the aesthetic though. 

Ohh, I also really love that the house was destroyed by the fireball, a nice touch! As a DM who loves maps, I am always swapping out damaged parts on my maps in games to try to show the destruction so it was delightful to see the environment change. 

and also nice sound design.

I don't know how but I see videos where it's like the game looked like this then i added lighting and post processing and it was the same exact art just made to look even better. I think this could look even better with some of that special sauce poured on it. I wish I had the way to do that to share, but I'm sure it can be looked up

replies.author: TheBigQuestion354
replies.body: I’ve actually been messing a bit with the lighting and saturation and you are correct. I actually noticed that it is quite washed out.

comments.author: Infinite-Switch6948
comments.body:
This looks cool, the animation is all a little herky jerky, at least with the camera movements and the dice rolling, it's just the timing all feels so mechanical, and like others have said the UI is an issue as with so many other AI games.

Overall looking awesome though and would definitely get my attention on Steam, because I also love some TTRPGs. 

In my game I am getting the armor to switch out (finally), I am modeling everything procedurally with opus and blender, but I had to kind of standardize the seams and measurements of where gloves/boots/legs/chest/head all are. It took forever for it to get working and it still all needs work but if you keep plugging away at it you can get it working.

What's your 3d process looking like? Blender? Meshy? Tripo?

replies.author: TheBigQuestion354
replies.body:
https://i.redd.it/hzndagvtxfzh1.jpeg

  
I have models that I actually made/painted, take a picture of them and send them to Astra to “clean them up”, then put them through Tripo. It makes awesome models and also I actually own the rights to them so that’s cool.

I am legit contemplating just learning Blender and posing the miniatures myself honestly for player characters changing weapons/armour. It is that frustrating.

replies.author: Infinite-Switch6948
replies.body:
I mean it sounds like a natural progression for you to learn to pose your own figures. I've seen a lot of workflows where people just get tripo to model elements of their armor and they assemble them and reshape them in blender.

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mmpLXA-xzrQ&t=10s](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mmpLXA-xzrQ&t=10s)

This guy is active in this community and has a great youtube channel. I think if you don't have to stress about animation and clipping and you are crafting armor for a single static figure you might be at an advantage in some ways, but you might have to refit every piece of armor for every type of figure build unless you can find a way to make it all modular.

replies.author: TheBigQuestion354
replies.body:
Watch his videos all the time!

You also making a TTRPG?
